recommendation: Keep the commit as a narrow correction to active build inputs. It does not reopen the status/adherence model or attempt a broader MedicationUsage sweep outside the seed's status-code wording defect.
issue_request: FHIR-39271 was a Published Pharmacy ballot issue resolved as Not Persuasive with Modification. The resolution kept the status redesign, renamed MedicationUsage back to MedicationStatement, confirmed that the status value set includes draft, and clarified that MedicationStatement.status is about the recording status of the statement while MedicationStatement.adherence carries taking/not-taking information.
initial_application: FHIR-32060 had already changed MedicationUsage.status to recorded, entered-in-error, and draft, with a note that those statuses differ from prior MedicationStatement statuses. FHIR-38682 later restored the MedicationStatement resource name and active fhir.ini entries, but that rename-back left one active status CodeSystem definition saying "medication usage" and left the status transition note as "MedicationStatement or MedicationStatement".
additional_context: FHIR-38682, FHIR-39329, and FHIR-39333 are the same Pharmacy status/adherence discussion family. Pharmacy minutes and the linked Zulip thread support the final model: the resource name is MedicationStatement, status is the statement record state, and adherence is the way to express taking, not-taking, on-hold, and stopped assertions.
reconciliation: Changed source/medicationstatement/codesystem-medication-statement-status.xml so the draft status definition says the medication statement is draft or preliminary, and changed source/medicationstatement/structuredefinition-MedicationStatement.xml so the status comment refers to previous releases of MedicationStatement without the duplicated name.
source_changes: source/medicationstatement/codesystem-medication-statement-status.xml: updated the draft code definition from medication usage to medication statement.
source/medicationstatement/structuredefinition-MedicationStatement.xml: fixed the MedicationStatement.status comment's malformed previous-release comparison.

related_jiras.note: Restored MedicationUsage to MedicationStatement and explains why the remaining status wording needed the restored name.
Established recorded, entered-in-error, and draft as the redesigned status codes.
Clarified that adherence covers taking/not-taking whether or not the patient was instructed or prescribed to take the medication.
Expanded the adherence example codes for on-hold and stopped cases.
